The Ultimate Motorcycle Touring Packing List

Forgetting essential items can ruin a tour. Our printable visual checklist covers everything you need across six categories so you never leave home without a critical item again.

1. Riding Gear

  • Helmet, Jacket, Trousers, Boots, Gloves, Base layers, Rain suit

2. Luggage

  • Panniers/saddlebags, Tank bag, Tail pack, Dry bags, Cargo net, Lock & chain

3. Tools & Spares

  • Tyre repair kit, Puncture plugs, Mini pump, Multi-tool, Spare fuses, Bulbs, Duct tape, Cable ties

4. Electronics

  • Phone mount, Sat nav, USB charger, Power bank, Camera, Intercom

5. Personal

  • First aid kit, Sun cream, Lip balm, Ear plugs, Tissues, Medications, Cash

6. Documents

  • Licence, Insurance, MOT cert, Breakdown cover card, Passport (if touring abroad)
Pro Tip: Pack heavy items low and close to the centre of gravity. Never strap anything to the handlebars.

keyTakeaways: The checklist covers six categories: riding gear, luggage, tools, electronics, personal items and documents.
Pack heavy items low and near the bike's centre of gravity for stable handling.
Never strap anything to the handlebars, as it affects steering.
Carry a tyre repair kit, mini pump and multi-tool for common roadside fixes.
Keep documents together: licence, insurance, MOT certificate and breakdown cover card.

faq.q: How should you distribute weight when packing a motorcycle?
faq.a: Pack heavy items low and as close to the bike's centre of gravity as possible, which keeps the handling stable and predictable. Lighter, bulky items can go higher in tail packs. Never strap luggage to the handlebars, as any weight there interferes with steering and can cause dangerous wobbles.

faq.q: What tools should you carry on a tour?
faq.a: A tyre repair kit with plugs, a mini pump or CO2 inflator, a pressure gauge, a multi-tool, spare fuses and bulbs, duct tape and cable ties cover the vast majority of roadside issues. These weigh very little and can be the difference between a quick fix and a long wait for recovery.

faq.q: What documents do I need for touring abroad?
faq.a: Carry your driving licence, insurance certificate, MOT certificate, V5C or a VE103 for a hired or financed bike, and your breakdown cover details. For trips outside the UK add your passport and check whether the destination requires a green card or an international driving permit before you set off.

faq.q: Should I use a printed or digital packing list?
faq.a: Either works, but a printed checklist you physically tick off is harder to skip through than a phone list. Many riders keep a laminated master copy in the garage. The key is to run through it methodically before every tour so nothing critical, such as your licence or first aid kit, gets left behind.

faq.q: What is the most commonly forgotten touring item?
faq.a: Chargers, breakdown cover cards and rain gear top the list of forgotten items. A power bank keeps your phone and sat nav alive when charging on the move fails, and packing your waterproofs where you can reach them at a moment's notice saves a soaking. Ear plugs are another frequent omission.
